candidates.source_title: Thieves break into deli and leave with a can of Fanta and a pack of cigarettes
candidates.source_summary: They didn't get away with much
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A deli in Rochdale was broken into but thieves only got away with a can of Fanta and a pack of cigarettes. Rachel Ward only opened the Healey Deli, on Market Street in Whitworth , back in October, but in a short space of time it has managed to build up a reputation for its sandwiches, breakfasts, drinks, and ice cream sundaes. In the early hours of Tuesday morning (August 18), Rachel claimed the shop door was broken into, with thieves smashing a window and using a crowbar to break into a till. But, posting on social media, Rachel said that the incident could have been much worse. Click here for the latest on Manchester's food & drink scene, gigs and more in our CityLife newsletter The cafe owner posted: “WELL… HEALEY DELI HAS OFFICIALLY MADE THE BIG TIME! Unfortunately, we had some unwanted visitors who decided to break into Healey Deli. “After smashing their way in, our criminal masterminds made off with… An emergency packet of cigarettes from the till and ONE Fanta Fruit Twist. That’s it. Not the food, not the coffee, not even the Spam. Apparently the getaway plan required a quick fag and a tropical fizzy drink.” In response to the post, some customers also took the opportunity to make light of the situation. One person posted: "What time do you open in the morning, knowing the spam is safe will pop in for a spam butty." Another said: "Awww Rach, really what was the point, all that damage and they didn't even kidnap the spam!" Despite seeing the funny side of the incident, Rachel told the Manchester Evening News that she was upset over the distress caused by the break-in and the damage that has been caused. She explained: "It is a shame that things like this happen. It is quite hurtful when someone comes in and damages your business that you’ve worked so hard on, especially all for pretty much nothing. We work hard, so it’s very frustrating. “We had to close the business for a day, we’re having to pay to get things repaired. It costs time and money to get these things all fixed and get back on track. It's just something we could have done without. “But I am also aware that there are worse things going on in the world. It’s one of those things where it’s just a case of having to move on from it - the show still goes on. “It has shown me how much of a real community spirit there is in the local neighbourhood. So many people have reached out to me to ask me if they can help me get my door fixed, or get security systems installed. It’s been very humbling.” Lancashire Police confirmed they had received a report of the incident, and are investigating the matter.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Students at St Anne’s Church of England Academy in Middleton are celebrating after the school matched the best GCSE results in its history. The Class of 2026 collected their results today, with this year’s outcomes on a par with the academy’s record-breaking results in 2025 — and continuing a significant period of improvement at the school. Among those celebrating was Adam Nowak, who achieved grades 8 and 9 across maths and the sciences and will now go on to study chemistry, physics and maths at Rochdale Sixth Form College. Adam said: “I don’t think I would be in this position without St Anne’s. All the teachers are really kind and are always happy to help. “I’ve achieved 8s and 9s in maths and the sciences, which are exactly the subjects I want to continue studying. St Anne’s has really helped me to get here.” For Erhun Osazuwa Erukpe, opening her results came as something of a shock, for all the right reasons. She said: “I was in shock when I saw my results. I did so much better than I expected. “At St Anne’s, the teachers are always really supportive. Even if you’re having a hard time, they are there to help you through it.”

candidates.source_title: Rochdale says goodbye to ‘a force for joy’ — the one and only Jimmy Cricket - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week. Jimmy died on August 3, aged 80, after a short illness with his family around him. Known for his clean humour, the Northern Ireland comedian became a household name in the 1970s after working the comedy club scene. Famous for his catchphrase “And there’s more”, he lived in Rochdale and was a big supporter of local charities and causes. On Thursday, August 20, his body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale from 3pm to 5pm on for anyone wanting to pay their respects. His life will then be celebrated at Salford Cathedral starting with a vigil mass for the reception of the body at 7pm. It will be followed by his funeral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at the cathedral, with mourners encouraged to wear bow ties which, along with his Wellington boots, became Jimmy’s trademark. candidates.source_body_excerpt: An illegal e-bike has been seized in Middleton town centre in a crackdown on anti-social behaviour. Officers from the Specialist Operations Unit have been carrying out proactive patrols in Middleton town centre following recent reports of anti-social behaviour around Middleton Bus Station and Middleton Gardens, including the misuse of electric bikes. At 7.30pm yesterday, officers on patrol in Middleton Gardens spotted a Sur-Ron style electric bike being ridden in the area. Officers detained the rider and seized the bike. A 16-year-old male was arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving, driving without a licence, driving without insurance and failing to provide a breath sample. He remains in custody for questioning. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Cardinal Langley RC High School is celebrating outstanding GCSE and BTEC results for the Class of 2026. More than 100 students have enrolled to continue their educational journey at Cardinal Langley, progressing into the Sixth Form to begin their A-level studies. This year saw a 10.6% increase in strong passes with 54.2% of all grades being 5 or above, along with a 6.2% increase in top grades with 19.2% of all grades being 7 or above. Students were welcomed by teachers, support staff, friends and family as they collected their results. Molly achieved a grade 9, a Distinction*, four grade 7s, a grade 6 and a grade 4. She will go on to study A levels in History, English and Politics. Alongside their GCSEs, students made an outstanding contribution to school life and the wider community, from completing their Duke of Edinburgh Awards and dedicating time to charity work, to achieving exceptional success in sport. They also demonstrated resilience, determination, compassion and a commitment to making a difference. Conrad who was not able to attend, achieved seven grade 9s, two grade 8s, a grade 7 and a Distinction* and will continue with A-level studies at Cardinal Langley. Headteacher Andrew Bridson, said: “Today has been a truly special morning and it was an absolute pleasure to welcome our students back to Cardinal Langley to celebrate with them. We are immensely proud of the results they have achieved and of the hard work, determination and perseverance that lie behind every one of them.

candidates.source_title: Oulder Hill records highest proportion of pupils achieving grades 9 to 5 in English and Maths
candidates.source_summary: Oulder Hill Leadership Academy has recorded its highest proportion of pupils achieving grades 9 to 5 in both English and Mathematics.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The Rochdale school said 50% achieved grades 9 to 5 in both subjects in this year’s GCSE results, while 67% secured grades 9 to 4.

Fatima Fahad was among the school’s highest-performing pupils, achieving four grade 9s, five grade 8s and a Level 2 Distinction.

Earlier this year, she received the Academic Excellence Award at the Rochdale Encouraging You Awards.

Fatima will now study Mathematics, Chemistry and Computer Science at Rochdale Sixth Form.

Her father said: “We have a long family history with Oulder Hill and have always worked well with the teachers who are extremely supportive. After COVID, she struggled, but the support and the school’s conversion to Star Academies has been transformational.”

Spencer Blackband achieved three grade 8s, including in English Language and English Literature, a grade 7 in Mathematics, a grade 6 in Photography and a Level 2 Merit in Digital IT. He also achieved strong passes in his other subjects.

He will study Biology, Geography and Mathematics at Rochdale Sixth Form.

Spencer said: “I am so grateful for the friends I have made and all of the support the school has given me, especially in Year 11.”

Head Girl Veronica Asnani achieved four grade 8s, two grade 7s, two grade 6s, a grade 5 and a Level 2 Distinction.

She spent part of the summer at Pembroke College at the University of Oxford, where the school said she experienced life as an Oxbridge student and delivered a talk to more than 200 delegates.

Veronica will continue her studies at Rochdale Sixth Form.

Deputy Head Boy Michael Tarran achieved one grade 9, six grade 8s, two grade 7s and a grade 6. He plans to study English Literature, Psychology and Film Studies.

Manahil Shaban, who joined Oulder Hill in Year 10 after moving to the UK, achieved a grade 9 in Urdu, a Level 2 Distinction and five grade 8s, including English, Mathematics and Science.

Principal Adi Smale said: “Today is a moment to recognise not only the excellent results our pupils have achieved, but the character, resilience and ambition they have shown throughout their time at Oulder Hill. These results are a testament to the hard work of our pupils, the dedication of our staff and the unwavering support of our families and wider school community.

The villages of Simister and Bowlee offer a rural lifestyle for local residents, surprisingly located next to one of the north west’s busiest motorway junctions – Simister Island. Sat right on the Bury/Rochdale border, the 98 hectares of farmland will effectively be transformed into a new village.

A new ‘local centre’, a primary school, bus routes, cycle ways and footpaths have all been touted for the project. The site would be delivered over several years and split into three parts – north, south and east, bisected by Heywood Old Road (the A6045). 

The southern parcel is expected to deliver around 800 homes, with 550 in the north and 200 in the east.

The ‘countryside beauty’ would be maintained throughout the site, according to the development framework, with green spaces and ‘pocket parks’ lining the walking and cycling routes throughout. 

The development framework claims this ‘active travel’ network would stretch as far as Heaton Park and link the site to surrounding towns and villages such as Simister next door, Middleton and Prestwich. Transport links to the impending Atom Valley development zone is also on the cards – offering connection to the estimated 20,000 new jobs.

Thousands more homes and the creation of vast amounts of industrial/work space is part of the major overhaul in the north eastern section of Greater Manchester. In Bury, Elton Reservoir is set to gain 3,500 new homes, with a further 1,250 planned for Walshaw. 

Including Simister Bowlee, this would total 6,300 new homes around the area. With this in mind, new transport links are seen as key to connecting the new homes to what is expected to become the largest and most accessible employment and innovation hubs in the region, driving substantial investment into Greater Manchester.

The latest development framework has set out how Simister Bowlee would fit into the wider plan for the region – called the Northern Gateway. 

Like many of the areas targeted in the Northern Gateway scheme, the site is not well served by public transport. It is expected to benefit from the proposed Metrolink extension to Middleton, but that is possibly decades away.

Road infrastructure improvements; bus route enhancements; and the creation of cycle and pedestrian routes would be created initially. The connections across the Atom Valley area would be expected to be established through a new Metrolink tram extension to Middleton and further afield after two decades of development.

The tram-train would be a new public transport vehicle that could travel on both rail lines and tram tracks, without being connected to the overhead lines.

Naturally, there is huge local objection to the major scheme. This is because 1,550 homes are going to be plonked between Simister and Bowlee.

candidates.source_title: £20m funding for underinvested areas of Rochdale set to be approved - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_summary: Forgotten areas on the edge of Rochdale are set for a makeover thanks to almost £20m in government cash.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Forgotten areas on the edge of Rochdale are set for a makeover thanks to almost £20m in government cash.

The council are set to accept the Pride in Place funding next week at the latest town hall meeting. This means the local authority would get the total £19.6m over the course of the next decade. 

It works out at just under £2m every year for 10 years. The targeted areas are Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield – all of which have been overlooked for funding historically.

Currently no plan has been created to decide on how the cash will be spent. However, tackling congestion; improving parking; creating new green spaces; enhancing local facilities; and expanding maternity services are all early suggestions being made.

At their meeting next week, town hall bosses are also set to approve the Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield Neighbourhood Board – who will establish the proposal on how to spend the money.

The Neighbourhood Board is made up of local community figures; MP Paul Waugh; the council’s regeneration boss Coun Daniel Meredith; and chaired by Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group.

According to council documents, they have until November 30, 2026 to submit their four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

This plan is necessary in order to unlock the funding. Some £150,000 has already been granted by the government in order to form the board and generate the plan.

When the Pride in Place funding was announced last year, there was understandable skepticism locally. This was due to the areas going years without proper investment. 

Ken Whittle has lived and worked in the area for decades. He felt very little investment has left the area looking tired and unloved.

Speaking previously, Ken said: “I’m very skeptical about this. People here are used to getting nothing.

“Something for the children will be good or a centre for the community to gather could work because, at the moment, that doesn’t exist.

“Social housing needs work so people can actually come in and have a home. We can’t let it go downhill any further.

“The hardest thing with this is that people are moving out because no one is doing anything with anything. There has been no investment really.

“Maybe this cash can change things, but it’s up to the community to do it properly.”

Another skeptic, Dinah Banks, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service: “I think people just get on with their own lives. Why bother, look at it, it’s got no life at the moment.

“I want to see better GP service and walk-in surgeries and not have to travel so far to get there.

“Maybe a proper community health service. But I won’t hold my breath.”

Rochdale MP Paul Waugh has already held consultation events with locals to get an understanding of what they want. 

Once the new Neighbourhood Board and government cash is formally accepted by Rochdale council’s cabinet on August 25, local views will shape how the future scheme looks.

candidates.source_title: Old industrial building demolition could unlock regeneration - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_summary: An old mill in Heywood will be demolished to make way for Heywood’s regeneration.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Regent Mill is an industrial complex rather than the typical historic cotton mill you see dominating the skylines of Rochdalian towns. But the bulldozing of this deteriorating building on St James Street could unlock a wider vision for Heywood.

Rochdale council, who are carrying out the demolition work, say they hope to bring forward plans to build around 200 new homes in this area of the town. 

These homes are expected to be more affordable homes. No timeline for when this could happen has been set out.

Once the former tile merchant has been levelled, it would facilitate housing schemes to come forward, according to the local authority. This would link into Heywood’s ongoing regeneration. 

A fresh new Heywood Civic has already been completed. This has been accompanied by the makeover to Peine Square on the Civic’s doorstep.

Some £20m of the government’s Pride in Place funding is currently being spent, with grant applications for local businesses expected to be open soon. This would bring further cash directly to local organisations to better the area.

Coun Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “The demolition of Regent Mill is part of the wider regeneration of this part of Heywood, as part of our masterplan. This will see us work with partners to transform brownfield sites around the town centre into new, high-quality much needed social homes for local people.

“Over time, we hope to bring forward more than 200 homes on and around the Regent Mill area. So where we now have empty sites, which are not visually appealing, we will have fantastic new homes to help address our housing shortage and give the whole area a lift. 

“We have already seen considerable regeneration within Heywood town centre and this project will continue this redevelopment and further support local families.”

There are some concerns about the demolition work raised by highways teams. Highways explained that recent demolitions of properties in this area ‘have caused damage to highways surfaces causing significant risk to pedestrians’.

Planning papers described how the council intends to fence off the demolition site, including debris netting and site signage to protect pedestrians and the roads.

Magdala Street has been made one way in the direction of Manchester Road, creating a one-way system at the top of Middleton Road at its junction with Charles Street in the direction of Manchester Road. But since its introduction last month, more than 200 residents have complained about traffic gridlock, near misses and damage to cars — and want the trial stopped. The council has received 242 individual responses to the scheme with 33 (14%) in-support and 209 (86%) objecting. The findings will be discussed at Heywood Township Committee’s extraordinary meting on Thursday, August 27, when many residents hope the plug will be pulled. But officers are recommending that committee continues the scheme for the full six-month trial.

candidates.source_title: Heywood's Pride in Place scheme without chair after Brian Davies steps down - Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_summary: Heywood's Pride in Place scheme without chair after Brian Davies steps down Roch Valley Radio
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The former chair for Heywood's Pride in Place scheme, Brian Davies, has stepped down, leaving the scheme temporarily without a chair for the £20 million initiative.

Elsie Blundell, MP for Heywood and Middleton North commented, saying: “Brian has done a fantastic job of getting the investment plan approved by government and starting the Pride in Place scheme.  Now it has to change to a delivery phase and it is exciting that we are looking for a new chair and two new board members to strengthen the board for this next important stage.

“We know that the community wants to see Pride in Place focus on three things: crime and anti-social behaviour, transport links, and facilities for young people. That’s what local residents have told us. Now we must deliver a transformation of the town, using this money.”

The Pride in Place project is led by the local community, with board members who represent different corners of Heywood's residents, community organisations, civil society, and businesses. After producing an investment plan and securing funding from the Government, the board is entering the project delivery phase, bringing forward and developing proposals for the £20m (£2m a year, for 10 years).

Elsie added:  “This is national money which can only be spent locally, led by the community.  It means an exciting new chapter in Heywood’s future to transform the town we see around us and create new opportunities for the people who live here.”

Heywood’s Pride in Place Board are looking for a new chair to lead the board through the next stage of its work, developing, and funding projects to shape the future of the town. They are also looking for two new members to join the board.

The Chair will lead engagement and keep Pride in Place focused on delivery through relationships with key stakeholder such as the Council, Rochdale Development Agency, the NHS, Action Together, and others.  Working with board members they will be responsible for sharing information, gaining consensus, and participation from the board and the community.

Elsie has said that anyone who is interested in applying can reach out to her office for a chat by emailing her. Elsie has said “We want a strong leader who is confidently about Heywood’s future, there is so much potential here.”

The deadline is 7th September.

“A deal was put on the table but taken away before we had chance to talk it over. We are ready to continue negotiations, but it’s obvious NCA has no intention of resolving this.

“This isn’t complicated. Staff are simply asking for what their contract says they’re entitled to. Nothing more.”

Staff from all four sites will gather in Salford on Wednesday 26th August for a unified day of protest.

candidates.source_title: Greater Manchester to receive £17m in funding to help with the homelessness crisis
candidates.source_summary: Through a £442 million package, the North West is to receive £37m to curb rough sleeping to get people in for the winter
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The Greater Manchester Combined Authority is to receive £16,955,174 over three years in an attempt to tackle rough sleeping in the area as part of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's national drive to end rough sleeping that totals £442 million across the country over three years, and £37 million in the North West.

The money is to create new accommodation and support that is to be rolled out across England this winter.

Alongside emergency accommodation for those who are rough sleepers, the programme will offer help with housing, health, and other needs, in an attempt to help people build a more stable future, rather than just giving people a temporary place to stay.

Accompanying this initiative, Burnham has announced that he will host a national summit in the Autumn to bring together leaders from business, finance, charities, health, faith communities, and more to ask what role each of them could play in ending rough sleeping.

Crisis, a charity for people who are homeless, suggest that preventing 40,000 people from becoming homeless could save the taxpayer close to £370 million.

PM Andy Burnham has said:  “No-one should have to bed down in a doorway or outside a station. But we’ve seen it for so long that it feels like Westminster has started to accept it.

"I won’t accept it. That’s why my first instruction as Prime Minister was to end rough sleeping. And it’s why today we’re getting started with a national drive to get everyone in for Christmas.

"We did it in the pandemic. We can do it again. But it needs all of us. Government will put the money in. But I’m asking leaders in communities and sectors across society to play their part locally too.

"Let’s get people out the cold. And let’s bring back hope."

Of the money in the initiative, £8.4 million of the new funding is going specifically to the Ending Homelessness in Communities Fund. This takes total funding allocations announced for 100 different projects to £47 million over three years.

As well as off the street provision, the funding will help local areas deliver more than 1000 settled homes over the next three years, alongside further wraparound support to help people rebuild their lives. Labour say that areas facing the greatest pressures will receive the largest share of support, with communities all across England getting support to address rough sleeping in their area.

Alongside funding allocations, the Government is publishing guidance to help local areas mobilise quickly and deliver a consistent route off the street offer this winter. The guidance will make clear the need to ensure adequate and accessible provision for women experiencing rough sleeping, recognising that women are often underrepresented in official statistics and may be at greater risk of violence, abuse, and exploitation. Guidance encourages local areas to consider single sex accommodation with specialist, intensive and trauma informed support, for victims of domestic abuse and sexual violence. This will support the government’s commitment to halve violence against women and girls in the next ten years.

This funding comes after Andy Burnham gave his first instruction to end rough sleeping across the country.

The agreement will see Rochdale Netball Club rebrand and become part of the club's wider 'Our Teams' family. The partnership brings together one of the borough's leading community sports clubs with its professional football club and official charitable arm, creating a stronger platform to grow netball and widen access to physical activity across Rochdale — from primary school participation through to junior and adult club netball, coaching, volunteering and leadership. Netball is one of the most widely played team sports in England, particularly among women and girls, with accessible formats for all ages and abilities, including junior netball, Back to Netball and Walking Netball. The agreement will also support wider community outcomes, with Rochdale AFC Community Trust working alongside Rochdale AFC Netball on new programmes in schools, holiday provision, health and wellbeing, and volunteer development. Operating under a shared Rochdale AFC identity opens up new opportunities too, from commercial support and matchday promotion to community events and sponsorship, reinforcing that women's sport has a central place in the borough's sporting future. The move follows a model seen elsewhere in professional sport, where football and rugby clubs have partnered with netball organisations to boost visibility, participation and long-term sustainability. In Rochdale, the priority will be a community-first approach that reflects the town's sporting pride and welcomes people of all ages.

MSV is a not-for-profit Registered Provider who own and manage almost 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire and West Yorkshire. 

The apartments would all be one-beds and the terraced homes would contain four-bedrooms each.

The site where the homes will be built currently sits empty. An old block of flats used to sit on the land next to the A664 (Queensway), but it was demolished in 2009. 

It was used as a temporary space by Kirkholt Medical Practice for a short time before the health centre got its permanent digs down the road.

Planning papers read: “The application site is a prominent site within the local area. The intention is to create a high-quality sustainable development that addresses housing needs and meets the needs of the local community.

“This proposal has been developed in response to an identified local demand, helping to reduce anti-social behaviour issues and the various problems associated with the site in its disused state.

“By redeveloping the former brownfield site, we plan on increasing the benefits of its regeneration by utilising vacant land and delivering affordable homes for local residents.

“MSV’s vision for this site is to create a secure outward looking scheme for social rent. They want to provide housing, with the aim of creating a balanced community and to promote tenure diversification in the area.”

Plans for a new community garden, to compliment the scheme, were also approved last month. It would be run by Q Gardens, a community group that already operates in the Kirkholt area.

Preparing for adulthood is about making the journey easier, clearer and more positive for young people aged 14 to 25, as well as the families and carers who support them. The council’s Preparing for Adulthood Team helps young people find the best support when moving from children’s services into adult social care. Before young people turn 18, the council completes an assessment to identify care and support needs. For those eligible, it will create new support plan to help young adults continue with their education, help them develop new skills and find any additional support the young person or their family might need. candidates.source_title: ‘This eviction is making us really ill’: The last couple standing on doomed Rochdale estate - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_summary: Lower Falinge was saved from demolition last year thanks to a legal challenge - but now revamped plans have come back
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The ominous wrecking ball looming over a 1960s housing estate in Rochdale has returned. Empty blocks on Lower Falinge were saved from the bulldozer 11 months ago following a successful legal challenge from campaigners. Now fresh demolition plans have been revealed. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) wants to knock down seven blocks of flats containing 150 homes and replace them with 270 new homes. The vision includes a mix of flats and houses on the land between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter In order to do this the maisonette blocks known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe and Vaynor all have to go. Only the Zedburgh block, also earmarked for demolition, is lived in. Andy Roche has been in Lower Falinge since 1988. Both he and his partner are the last holdouts in the Zedburgh block. They are ‘distraught’ by the latest news. They knew this was coming though. When RBH was stopped from demolishing the blocks last year, they were told they needed to showcase what they would actually do with the land - rather than just leave it grassed over. Although a new vision has now been revealed, it doesn’t make it any easier for Andy. Andy said: “Obviously it’s extremely distressing for me because it involves being forced out of my home. I am not happy about RBH’s proposals, but I’m not sure how to put it into words. “I’m still processing it. I don't believe they have listened to the residents of the estate at all. “My partner is also distraught. We are both autistic and this eviction is making us both really ill.” So many tenants have upped sticks and moved on, but for Andy this estate has everything he wants. He has been offered multiple different housing options by RBH, but none of them have lived up to what he currently has, he claims. Last year Andy provided a tour of the estate. Walking through the maze of flats, it looked desolate The Newstead block overlooks the communal grassland, every window boarded up with plywood. This indicated the vandalism the area suffers. Andy points out how families can watch their children play on the grass outside from through their living room windows. But there are no children here anymore, and no families. RBH says the blocks are no longer fit for purpose and have lived way beyond their life span. The social housing landlord says their new plans have been informed by the consultation of local residents. The estate is a bizarre clash of old and new though. Opposite the Ollerton block, next door to Andy’s Zeburgh block - there is a brand new play park surrounded by plush new housing. This is part of the previous phases of the overarching redevelopment already carried out by RBH. They have already delivered 100 new homes in Lower Falinge after previous demolition work. The previous phases began with demolition work in 2012, a year after Lower Falinge was named the most deprived area in England for the fifth year running. The estate took another hammering in 2016 when former Prime Minister David Cameron called it a sink estate - meaning a place that suffers from severe social and economic deprivation. That upset Andy upset. Many in his shoes would think a visit from the Prime Minister would bring hope for the future. What saddens him more is seeing the blocks that used to be full of life look derelict and silent. Seeing the blocks such as Pershore and Stavordale get refurbished to avoid damp and mould problems

candidates.source_body_excerpt: US actress Hayden Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. A representative for the actress confirmed the death to US network ABC News on Sunday, saying her family would remember her “incredible light” who brought “immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her”. The statement from her father Skip read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.” Her father also asked that her family be given privacy as they “take time to process this unimaginable loss”. No cause of death has been announced. The 36-year-old began acting as a child, appearing in soap operas before gaining wider recognition for her role in the 2000 sports drama Remember The Titans alongside Denzel Washington, and as the voice of Dot in 1998’s A Bug’s Life. Panettiere later found fame playing cheerleader Claire Bennet in the superhero drama Heroes before going on to star as up-and-coming country singer Juliette Barnes for six seasons on the hit TV series Nashville. Her film credits include 2006’s Bring It On: All Or Nothing, comedy-drama film Raising Helen, and appearances in Scream 4 and Scream VI as Kirby Reed. Following her rapid rise to fame, the pressure of the industry began to weigh on Panettiere – with the actress previously revealing that she had struggled with addiction throughout her 20s. In a memoir published earlier this year, Panettiere opened up about her struggles with mental health, the loss of her younger brother, Jansen, and her decision to give full custody of her daughter to her former partner, Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A retired police officer has returned to his old station more than 60 years after starting his career. Allan Murray, now 93, visited Rochdale police station to share memories from his time as an officer, which began in 1959 when he joined the force at the age of 22. During his visit, Mr Murray brought a collection of photographs and stories from his years in service, including images from his training at Bruche Police Training Centre. A photo of PC Allan Murray's during his career (Image: Greater Manchester Police) His great-granddaughter, PC Sophie Brown, currently serves with Greater Manchester Police and is also based in Rochdale. PC Brown said: "I’ve always had so much respect and love for my great grandad. "I’ve been so grateful to follow in his footsteps and honour him in the career that I’m doing. "It was amazing to be able to show him around the station and bring him back to his ‘good old days’.
